intended_object: The strict superlevel set {x ∈ ℝ : Tf(x) > α} of the nonnegative function Tf, for an operator T acting on Schwartz functions. This is the set whose measure appears on the left of the weak-type / Φ-modular estimate |{Tf > α}| ≤ C ∫ Φ(|f|/α). Inferred from the docstring and from its use in `HasSchwartzPhiModularEstimate`.
explanation:
The body is `{x | ENNReal.ofReal α < T f x}`, which is exactly the strict superlevel set {Tf > α}. The comparison happens in ℝ≥0∞ because T takes values there, so infinite values of Tf are correctly counted as exceeding α. For α ≤ 0, `ofReal α = 0` and the set becomes {Tf > 0}. This differs from the literal {Tf > α}, which would be all of ℝ, but the library only uses the definition with α > 0 (in `HasSchwartzPhiModularEstimate`), where it agrees with the intended object, so this is harmless.

The definition is tied to the library's `SchwartzNonnegativeOperator` structure on 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ), which is the setting of the paper's estimate. It is a thin named wrapper, not a general construction that Mathlib provides in a broader setting. Mathlib has no dedicated named superlevel-set definition; the set-builder form is the standard idiom. So the definition is faithful.
